topic: Your Model Didn't Decay. Your Data Pipeline Did.
postText:
We watched model accuracy drop 22% over six weeks. The knee-jerk reaction: retrain. We did. Accuracy barely moved. That's when we realized the model wasn't decaying—our feature pipeline was silently sending garbage.

A upstream schema change turned a nullable column into a string. Our preprocessing code coerced it to NaN. The model kept predicting, just badly. No errors. No alerts. Just quiet degradation.

Here's the architecture pattern that saved us:

1. Feature-level monitoring. Track distributions (mean, null rate, cardinality) per feature, not just final accuracy. Accuracy is a lagging indicator. Feature drift is leading.

2. Contract tests in CI. Every feature schema gets a test: types, ranges, nullability. Upstream change breaks the build, not production.

3. Shadow retraining. New model runs on live traffic in parallel before promotion. Compare outputs, then swap. Never deploy blind.

The lesson: ML observability is data observability. Your model is innocent until proven guilty. The pipeline is usually the culprit.

What's your go-to signal that tells you it's a model problem versus a data problem? Have you been burned by silent feature drift? Drop your war stories in the comments.

If this resonated, like, comment your experience below, and share this with a teammate who's chasing ghosts in their model metrics. Follow @pengikut for more production AI architecture lessons.
